customManagers.description: The Build-Depends floor in debian/control. No manager covers it, and it was wrong for months — it asked for golang-go 1.21 while the code already needed 1.25 for http.NewCrossOriginProtection. Versioning is `docker`, not `npm`: these pins carry two components, and `1.26` is not a valid semver version — under npm versioning Renovate found the dependency, listed it on the dashboard and returned an empty candidate set, so the first real toolchain bump moved go.mod and the Dockerfile and silently left every pin below behind. Docker versioning treats a truncated version as a version.

packageRules.description: Patch updates: auto-merge after CI passes

Minor updates: manual review. This is a firewall — the blast radius of a bad dependency is the host's packet filter, so the conservative half of the house style applies here, as it does on the ansible box.
Major updates: manual review, attach release notes

Every place the Go toolchain is written moves in ONE pull request. Without this the repository returns to the state that prompted the migration: the Dockerfile on 1.26 because Dependabot could read a Docker tag, and go.mod plus ten workflow steps on 1.25 because it could not read those. go.mod's toolchain line is the source; the Dockerfile tag, debian/control and the prose pins follow it through the customManagers above. Never auto-merged, whatever the update type says: this is the compiler that builds a packet filter, and it also needs `npm run build:diagrams` for the install-choice picture.
prBodyNotes: Re-render the diagrams after merging this: `npm run build:diagrams` — `docs/_diagrams/install-choice.mmd` names the Go version and the rendered SVGs carry a digest of it.
`internal/shared/go_version_test.go` fails if any of the places that write the toolchain down disagree, so CI proves this PR is complete.

packageRules.description: The go directive is the minimum language version this module claims, not the toolchain we build with. Raising it costs every consumer, and Go's own guidance is to leave it where it is; it moves when the code starts using a newer API. Renovate does not propose it by default — this states that on purpose, so nobody adds rangeStrategy:bump later without meeting the reason.
htmx is copied into web/static/htmx.min.js by hand and CI compares the two, so a bump without the copy step fails the assets job.
mermaid renders the committed diagrams and its version is folded into their digest, so an upgrade makes every SVG stale by design — see scripts/render-diagrams.mjs.
prBodyNotes: Run after merging: `npm run build:diagrams` — every diagram is stale until then, and the assets job says so.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A fix for a known vulnerability does not wait for the nightly window. GitHub's own 'Dependabot security updates' setting is switched off in favour of this, so one tool raises the pull request rather than two raising it for the same advisory. The alerts themselves stay on — they are what this reads.
